fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the entry point, particularly at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles along its length so responders can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Designate and keep clear a flat area near the main residence where emergency vehicles can turn around, and communicate its location to responding crews.
• Trim dense vegetation along the sides of the access drive so that large emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back any vegetation that blocks sightlines at the driveway entrance so drivers pulling onto the road have a clear view of approaching traffic.
• Mark or label the detached structure visibly from the access drive so responders arriving on scene can quickly identify it as a separate building.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move quickly on foot between the two buildings.
• Keep any gates along the access drive unlocked or secured with a Knox-type lock so responders are not delayed reaching either structure.
• Trim dense vegetation near both structures to maintain clear space around exterior walls so responders can move around each building.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Remove dead grass and dry plant material from around the base of the house.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure so individual trees are no longer touching each other with their branches.
• Cut grass short across the open areas surrounding the structure, particularly between the tree clusters and the house.
• Separate shrubs scattered around the structure from nearby trees by removing or trimming vegetation that connects them.
• Remove low-hanging branches on trees closest to the house so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear the single access route of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and any debris that would slow entry or exit.
• Widen cleared ground on both sides of the driveway so a fire truck can pass without vegetation contact.
• Thin scattered trees between the open terrain and the house to break up the continuous path of vegetation leading toward the structure.
• Keep the area immediately around any outbuildings or detached structures clear of shrubs, tall grass, and dead plant material.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the road.
• Maintain short, mowed grass in the open terrain areas closest to the structure rather than allowing it to grow tall and dry.
